title: Market-aware routing, budget fencing, and instance-class selection
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a market-aware routing layer that selects region + instance-class combinations based on real-time price signals, spot eviction risk, tenant budget caps, and application SLO tiers. The feature should support graceful fallback to cheaper model variants (quantized / trimmed context) and automatic budget fencing for tenants with spend limits.

Goals:
- Reduce average per-token cost for workloads flagged as cost-sensitive without increasing latency SLO breaches for P0 tenants.
- Provide deterministic spend caps per-tenant with soft and hard enforcement modes.
- Route requests to the best region/accelerator SKU given: spot price delta, historical eviction rate, model variant compatibility, and tenant preferences.
- Allow safe fallbacks: (1) model variant fallback (e.g., fp16 -> int8 -> trimmed-arch), (2) region fallback, (3) throttling to preserve a tenant's hard cap.

Success metrics (first 8 weeks):
- 12% reduction in cost-per-token for P2 workloads flagged as cost-sensitive (measured on representative production traffic).
- <0.5% increase in 90th-percentile latency for P0 tenants.
- No more than 1 customer-visible overrun per 10k capped-tenant requests for soft caps; 0 overruns for hard caps.
- Telemetry: new per-tenant spend-breakdown and routing-decision traces available in Console.

Scope / Non-goals:
In scope:
- Routing decision service and policy engine, region/sku scoring, budget fencing, model-variant compatibility matrix, operator controls in Console.
- Config schema for per-tenant policy: priority tier, soft/hard cap, preferred regions, allow-spot flag, preferred SKUs.
Out of scope for this ticket:
- New kernel/quantization codegen (we use existing quantized runtime paths).
- Billing pipes changes (we emit usage events; billing team has separate integration ticket).

Technical approach:
1) Scoring engine: periodic price/eviction fetchers (cloud APIs + internal spot telemetry) produce a normalized "cost-risk" score per region+sku. Scores are time-series; we keep 1min granularity and 7d rolling stats.
2) Policy evaluation: for each incoming request, we compute a routing score that combines tenant policy (priority, allow-spot, budget headroom), model compatibility (tokenizer/context limits, quantization support), and real-time cost-risk. Tunable weights: w_cost, w_risk, w_latency_penalty, w_tenant_priority.
3) Variant plan: when the best-scoring path violates a tenant's hard cap, or risk >= THRESHOLD, the evaluator consults the model-variant graph for degradations (e.g., full -> int8 -> small_variant). Each variant has an expected quality delta and a modeled latency/cost profile.
4) Budget fencing: two modes:
   - soft: allow a proportion of requests to exceed soft cap but emit warning traces and reduce preference for on-demand SKUs; triggers a "throttle window" if overruns climb.
   - hard: reject/queue requests once the hard cap is reached; return structured error with spend metadata and suggested retry window.
5) Caching and batching interplay: routing decisions for cached prefixes reuse previous route decisions for the prefix duration. Batching scheduler signals expected throughput to the evaluator so it can pre-warm allocations in a region.

API / Config model (draft):
- tenant.routing_policy: {"priority_tier":"P0|P1|P2","allow_spot":true|false,"preferred_skus":["A100","H100","T4"],"soft_cap_cents":12345,"hard_cap_cents":15000,"fallback_strategy":"model-variant,region,throttle"}
- route_query flags: request.priority_override, request.quality_target (e.g., 0.95), request.max_latency_ms.

Implementation notes:
- New service: route-evaluator (stateless, k8s autoscaled). Maintains ephemeral cache of cost-risk and model-variant metadata. Publishes decision traces to trace pipeline.
- Persistent store: policy store in existing config-db (reads cached with TTL). Budget windows are tracked in a Redis time-series counter per-tenant and reset aligned to billing windows.
- Control plane: Console feature to set caps and preview simulated impact on recent traffic (traffic replay sandbox).

Testing & rollout plan:
- Unit tests: score aggregation, policy evaluation, variant graph traversal.
- Integration tests: end-to-end with staging runtime endpoints (mock spot API with eviction events).
- Canary rollout: 5% of non-P0 traffic with telemetry gating. Metrics gate: cost reduction >= 5% and <1% increase in P0 latency.
- Ops runbook: steps to disable spot routing globally, enforce hard-only caps, and rollback route-evaluator.

Monitoring & Alerts:
- Dashboards: per-tenant spend vs cap, route decision heatmap (region/sku choices), variant degradation counts, cap-enforcement events.
- Alerts: >0.1% hard-cap rejections for P1/P0 tenants, >5% spike in variant degradations, sudden increase in spot eviction rate in a region.

Risks and mitigations:
- Quality regressions if variant graph incorrectly maps to degraded models. Mitigation: require quality validation jobs and manual approvals per variant pair.
- Billing mismatches for soft cap overshoots. Mitigation: emit pre-billing notices and retain request traces for repro.
- Thundering migrations to cheaper regions causing capacity pressure. Mitigation: throttled shift with concurrency ramps and backpressure signals from region allocator.

Open questions:
- Should we allow tenant-defined cost-weighting DSL (e.g., prefer lower latency up to X% more cost)? (prefers product discussion)
- Exact backoff policy when region capacity becomes constrained while budget headroom exists.

Acceptance criteria:
- route-evaluator serves production traffic for non-P0 tenants behind a feature flag and honors soft/hard cap semantics.
- Console shows per-tenant projected monthly spend after enabling a policy.
- Automated tests cover policy edge cases and variant fallthrough logic.
updates: 2026-03-02: Architecture review with Runtime and Billing teams. Decided to keep billing integration as emit-events; Billing will consume events and reconcile. Action: ENG-271829 created for billing integration.
2026-03-04: Design doc posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RTE/Market-Aware+Routing+spec. Requesting security review for cross-region policy enforcement.
2026-03-06: Implemented initial cost-risk fetcher (mock cloud API). Benchmarked aggregation: 1k region-sku entries processed in 80ms per cycle. Added unit tests for score normalization.
2026-03-09: Spike showed that naive spot re-routing increased eviction exposures for P1 traffic during simulated cloud maintenance. Added risk-weight parameter and gating for P1/P0.
2026-03-11: route-evaluator prototype deployed to staging behind feature flag. Integration tests with runtime passed. Canary plan drafted.
2026-03-13: PM approval for canary. Assigned Diego to lead production canary and Maya to own Console controls. Next: finalize variant compatibility matrix and add per-variant quality metrics to CI.
